title: Introduce harmonic ensemble deconvolver and tenant-aware fallback for perf canaries
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Add a new Harmonic Ensemble Deconvolver (HED) component to the perf-canary pipeline. HED fuses three orthogonal detectors (spectral drift, temporal-windowed percentile shifts, and traffic-shape-conditioned residuals) and applies a lightweight deconvolution step to separate short-lived noise harmonics (traffic burst and probe artifacts) from persistent regressions. The goal is to reduce false-positive canary alerts while preserving sensitivity to real throughput/latency regressions and to provide a tenant-aware fallback that keeps rollouts moving during noisy traffic windows.

Motivation and context: Over the last 6 months we observed a ~18% false-positive rate in canary alerts for tail-latency regressions that correlate with short-lived client-side spikes and synthetic-probe alignment issues. Existing single-signal detectors either overreact to traffic harmonics or under-detect gradual degradations. HED addresses both by: 1) deconvolving periodic noise components using a compact harmonic filter; 2) combining detectors in an ensemble using a weighted consensus that is calibrated per-tenant and per-route; 3) exposing a controlled fallback policy that temporarily softens cutover thresholds (graceful corking) while creating a prioritized re-probing schedule.

What this PR changes:
- New component: perf_canary/detectors/harmonic_ensemble.py implementing the harmonic decomposition, consensus logic, and per-tenant weighting lookup.
- Integration: pipeline stages updated to call HED between metric-aggregation and canary-evaluator. This includes a new API hook canary.pipeline.deconvolve(metrics, tenant_id).
- Rollout guard extension: add a tenant-aware fallback policy that reduces new traffic weight if HED reports high harmonic-contamination but low consensus severity. Fallback is configurable via canary policies: .fallback.window_seconds and .fallback.max_soft_percentage.
- Telemetry: new metrics hed.harmonic_contamination_ratio, hed.consensus_score, hed.deconvolved_latency_p90 and corresponding tracing spans for attribution.
- Tests: unit tests for harmonic decomposition, ensemble weighting, and an end-to-end integration test using historical traffic replayer; added canary harness fixtures to simulate tenant-specific noise.
- Documentation: docs/perf-canary/HED-design.md and short guide in docs/operator/runbooks/canary-fallbacks.md.

Design highlights and tradeoffs:
- The harmonic filter is intentionally low-compute (FFT over rolling window with fixed N=128) so it can run in the pipeline without requiring additional workers. We avoid full spectral-learning to keep memory bounded.
- Ensemble weights are initialized from historical baseline and are updated weekly by a background calibrator job (not in this PR). The PR includes the hooks for weight refresh.
- Fallback policy is conservative: it only decreases route cutover weight up to a configurable soft percentage and requires HED to report contamination for at least two consecutive evaluation windows to take effect. This prevents oscillation during multi-minute traffic shifts.

Testing and results:
- Unit: 26 new unit tests, coverage +2.1% for perf-canary package.
- Integration: ran the synthetic traffic replay for 48 hours on staging (traffic mix A/B/C) and ran 72-hour historical backfills across 12 tenants. Results: false-positive alerts reduced by 45% (relative) for tail-latency regressions attributed to short-lived bursts; true positive detection latency for sustained degradations improved by 30% (median). No measurable adverse impact on throughput or CPU on canary pipeline workers (avg +3% CPU, p95 unchanged).
- Chaos test: injected client-side bursts and probe misalignment for two tenants; HED prevented unnecessary rollback in both cases and re-scheduled probes which discovered the regressions as persistent and then triggered normal rollback after 8-12 minutes.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation of HED algorithm and ensemble consensus.
- [x] Pipeline integration and API hook.
- [x] Unit & integration tests.
- [x] Metrics/tracing instrumentation.
- [x] Documentation and runbook updates.
- [x] Reviewed and approved by perf and sre.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- HED is gated behind a config flag canary.features.harmonic_ensemble=false by default. We will enable it for a small subset of tenants on staging for 48h, then enable on 10% of traffic on lower prod and monitor hed.consensus_score and alert rates for 72h before full rollout.
- No breaking changes: the canary evaluator API remains stable; the deconvolution step is additive.

Risks and mitigation: 
- Risk: under-detection if ensemble weights are miscalibrated for a tenant. Mitigation: fallback policy is conservative and background calibrator will tune weights; ops can revert via feature flag.
- Risk: increased CPU on pipeline workers. Mitigation: harmonic filter uses tuned N=128 and early-exit heuristics; metrics added to watch CPU and queue length.

Related work: This complements the temporal-windowed and percentile-weighted detectors introduced earlier (see ENG-1553 and PRs in this repo). It is intentionally orthogonal to the latency-cliff detector; HED reduces noise that often causes spurious cliff detections.

How to review: Focus on detector correctness (harmonic_ensemble.py), unit tests in tests/perf_canary/test_harmonic_ensemble.py, and the limited API changes in pipeline.py. Trace examples and graphs are in docs/perf-canary/HED-examples.png.

release_notes: Add Harmonic Ensemble Deconvolver to perf canary pipeline: reduces false positives due to short-lived traffic harmonics, introduces tenant-aware soft fallback policy, and adds HED telemetry. Disabled by default behind feature flag.
